processing_steps.reduction_ratio: forged to a forging blank with cross section of about 40 mm × 60 mm
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingot of the Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C steel (20 kg, prepared by vacuum induction melting) was heated to 1200 °C and forged to a forging blank with cross section of about 40 mm × 60 mm.
The forging blank was homogenized at 1200 °C for 1 h before hot rolling.

processing_steps.cooling_medium: water quenched to about 300 °C (then air cooled)
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: hot-rolled to a plate of 3 mm thickness
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Parent process (proc_hr). The homogenized blank was hot-rolled to a 3 mm plate, finishing rolling temperature around 880 °C, then water quenched to about 300 °C.
Defining step of this sample: the hot-rolled plate was annealed at 950 °C for 1 h, followed by water quenching (one condition of the 700–1200 °C series).

structures.overall_structure: Banded microstructure consisting of ferrite (α) and austenite (γ); no obvious κ-carbide resolvable in the matrix, but small boundary κ-carbide formed during quenching along some large α grains (α/α boundaries); the banded structure persists but is less contiguous, and α and γ grains have coarsened relative to lower annealing temperatures.

phases_present.morphology: continuous banded large α grains (α2, from solidification/casting) plus fine α grains (α1) distributed among γ grains
phases_present.grain_size: α1 (ferrite among γ grains) 2.5 μm at 950 °C

phases_present.volume_fraction: about 60% (γ fraction stays in the 57%–63% range for 900–1200 °C)
not detected by XRD (boundary κ-carbide too small)
phases_present.morphology: small boundary κ-carbide films formed during quenching along α/α boundaries of some large α grains; no obvious matrix κ-carbide in the matrix

defects.type: dislocations inherited from hot rolling (progressively eliminated with higher annealing temperature)

average_grain_size.value: 2.5 μm (α1, ferrite mainly distributed among γ grains, at 950 °C)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: γ phase and banded α2 coarsen strongly above 900 °C; fine α1 among γ grains grows little until above 1000 °C (α1 dips slightly between 900 and 950 °C).

precipitates.distribution: along α/α boundaries of some large α grains in the α area

phase_interfaces.phase_2_name: ferrite (α) (α/α boundary decorated with boundary κ-carbide)

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Microcracks preferentially initiate around κ-carbide, which is detrimental to the tensile properties; the boundary κ-carbide along some large α grains is believed to be detrimental to ductility.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: secondary cracking along the banded microstructure
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Large secondary cracks are well developed in all annealed specimens and are believed to be related to the banded microstructure; the fracture mode is a mixture of ductile fracture of γ and quasi-cleavage fracture of α.

interfaces.phase_evolution: At 950 °C the matrix κ-carbide has completely dissolved during annealing (dissolution temperature between 850 °C and 900 °C); small boundary κ-carbide re-forms during quenching along α/α boundaries. No obvious kappa-carbide is resolvable in the matrix.
interfaces.interface_notes: The N–W orientation relationship between κ-carbide and α matrix is reported for the lamellar κ at 700 °C and for boundary κ at 1200 °C; it is not specifically documented for the 950 °C specimen.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gage length 50 mm, gage width 12.5 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile axis parallel to the rolling direction; specimens machined from the annealed and water quenched plate; tested on a universal testing machine (CMT 4105).

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–engineering strain curve of the 950 °C, 1 h specimen (Fig. 15(a)) and its true stress–true strain curve (Fig. 15(b)); the curve shows continuous yielding (no yield phenomenon) and lies below the lower-temperature curves.
tensile_properties.strain_hardening_rate: For specimens annealed at 900 °C and 950 °C, the work hardening rates are similar, but the 950 °C specimen fractured (snapped) earlier.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku D/Max-RB, Cu target operated at 40 kV and 150 mA
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify constituent phases (α, γ, κ) and determine phase volume fractions using the direct comparison method; determine lattice parameters.
characterization_methods.key_findings: κ-carbide peaks are absent in the 950 °C specimen (and HR ≥900 °C); only α and γ reflections present. Boundary κ-carbide in the 900–1200 °C range is too small to be detected by XRD.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Mechanically polished and etched in 8% Nital
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine the banded microstructure and phase distribution of annealed specimens.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Banded structure persists; at 900 °C and above the bands become less continuous and coarser with no obvious κ-carbide.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Quanta 450 operated at an acceleration voltage of 20 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Secondary-electron imaging; specimens etched in 8% Nital; grain sizes measured with ImageJ software
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine microstructure/phases and measure grain sizes of annealed specimens; examine boundary κ-carbide and quench-formed FCC particles.
characterization_methods.key_findings: No κ-carbide resolvable in the matrix of the 950 °C specimen; α and γ grains coarsened; small α grains among γ grains; grain boundaries clearly outlined.

characterization_methods.technique: transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with selected-area diffraction (SADP)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL 2100 operated at an acceleration voltage of 200 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Thin foils prepared by twin-jet polishing in 10% perchloric acid + 90% alcohol at −30 °C and 30 V
characterization_methods.purpose: Confirm phases, orientation relationships (e.g. N–W) between κ-carbide and α matrix, and examine boundary κ-carbide and deformation structures.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Ordering of atoms in α or γ is not expected during 700–1200 °C/1 h annealing; boundary κ-carbide confirmed between large α grains (900–1200 °C range).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EDS attached to the FE-SEM (FEI Quanta 450)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Line scans across phase regions during SEM observation (performed on 800 °C and 900 °C specimens)
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine the chemical composition of phases and elemental partitioning between α, γ and κ-carbide.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Mn and Al contents are highest in κ-carbide; Mn higher and Al lower in γ compared with α; Al K ~11 wt.% and Mn K ~10–14 wt.% at κ positions with Fe depletion.

characterization_methods.technique: grain size measurement from SEM micrographs
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure average grain sizes of α1, α2 and γ as a function of annealing temperature (900–1200 °C).
characterization_methods.key_findings: γ increases from 5.5 μm to 36.0 μm and α2 from 26.1 μm to 68.4 μm over 900–1200 °C; α1 decreases from 3.2 μm to 2.5 μm from 900 to 950 °C.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Equilibrium phase fractions of ferrite (α), austenite (γ) and κ-carbide (κ) computed for the Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C steel above 550 °C; fractions based on atomic fraction.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated κ-carbide solvus (823 °C) is lower than the experimentally observed dissolution temperature (between 850 °C and 900 °C); the general trend of phase fractions agrees with the XRD-measured volume fractions. Differences attributed to non-equilibrium state and atomic-vs-volume-fraction basis.

analytical_models.equation_role: Predicts equilibrium phase fractions (α, γ, κ, liquid) versus temperature
analytical_models.model_note: Computed with the TCFE7 database; used for comparison with measured phase evolution.

unmapped_findings: Product of strength and ductility for the 950 °C/1 h specimen = 21 GPa% (ultimate strength × ultimate elongation), from Table 1 (b0065, table_001).
The 950 °C, 1 h specimen shows continuous yielding (no yield-point phenomenon), like the other annealed specimens except the 700 °C one (b0035, b0061).
For specimens annealed at 900 °C and 950 °C, the work hardening rates are similar, but the 950 °C specimen snapped (fractured) earlier than the 900 °C specimen (b0035).

At 950 °C the ultimate strength and yield strength continue the monotonic decreasing trend with annealing temperature, while the ultimate elongation is past its peak (peak at 900 °C) and decreasing (b0037, b0060, figure_016).
γ phase volume fraction is about 57%–63% over the 900–1200 °C range, reaching the largest value (~63%) around 1000 °C and decreasing slightly to ~57% at 1200 °C (b0033, b0053).
Dissolution temperature of κ-carbide is between 850 °C and 900 °C (higher than the Thermo-Calc value of 823 °C); thus no matrix κ-carbide is expected in the 950 °C specimen (b0008, b0033, b0052).

In Table 2 the present steel (best condition, 900 °C) is compared with other Fe–Mn–Al–C steels; the present steel has the lowest ultimate elongation (36.6%) and the lowest product of strength and ductility (31 GPa%) among the listed steels. Note these comparison values correspond to the 900 °C condition, not directly to the 950 °C sample (b0071, table_002).

EDS line-scan elemental partitioning (κ-carbide richest in Mn and Al; γ richer in Mn and lower in Al than α) was performed only on the 800 °C and 900 °C specimens, not on the 950 °C specimen (b0032, figure_013).
